comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find the place preference control experiment (C81-C83) and its interpretation (C148-C149, C151) to be well-supported. OpenEval notes this addresses a critical confound from prior literature, while peer reviewers explicitly praise this as ruling out aversive memory formation.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations strongly support the temporal specificity findings from the offset control (C121-C124). OpenEval emphasizes this strengthens the interpretation of timing-dependent effects, while peer reviewers explicitly praise the offset control design as a methodological strength.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the main summary conclusions (C100-C101, C116-C117, C150). OpenEval notes convergence of stimulation and inhibition results, while peer reviewers affirm this as an important study with solid evidence. Both find the synthesis of findings well-supported.

Agreement on uncertainty. Both evaluations acknowledge the incomplete infection limitation (C11, C84, C134-C135). OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN due to speculation about infection rates, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this limitation and note the need for pathway-specific targeting.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the durability findings at one week (C68-C77). OpenEval emphasizes parallel statistical evidence and lasting enhancement, while peer reviewers affirm the long-term nature of extinction memory enhancement without questioning the one-week results.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the reduced spontaneous recovery findings (C58-C67). OpenEval notes comprehensive statistical evidence and convergence of analyses, while peer reviewers accept these findings without critique and affirm the inhibition of spontaneous recovery.

Strong agreement. Both evaluations support the finding that LC stimulation has no immediate effect on extinction performance (C6, C53-C57). OpenEval emphasizes this establishes effects on retention rather than acquisition, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm no effect during extinction but impact on expression through decreased spontaneous recovery.

Agreement on methodological validity. Both evaluations support combining TH-Cre and wild-type controls based on behavioral equivalence (C43-C46, C164-C165). OpenEval provides detailed statistical justification, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this by not questioning the approach.

Divergence in certainty level. OpenEval rates the LC inhibition null results (C10, C89-C99) as SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting unclear LC-NA behavior during extinction and questioning whether the null result reflects true absence of effect or methodological limitations.

Partial overlap on LC inhibition acute effects. OpenEval focuses on the immediate effect during extinction sessions (C9, C84-C88) and rates as SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers combine acute and long-term inhibition results and express uncertainty about interpretation, noting unclear LC-NA behavior and possible anti-extinction role.

OpenEval identifies speculative explanations for null results (C126-C130, C136-C138) and rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct empirical support. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative mechanistic claims.

OpenEval evaluates background theoretical concepts on extinction (C1-C3, C13-C16) as SUPPORTED by prior literature. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these background claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluates prior pharmacological literature establishing rationale (C4, C17-C20) as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these background citations, treating them as accepted context.
OpenEval evaluates anatomical and electrophysiological background (C21-C27) as SUPPORTED by prior literature. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these foundational claims.
OpenEval evaluates summary of inconsistent prior findings (C28-C34) as SUPPORTED and appropriately motivating the study. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate this literature review component.
OpenEval evaluates the identification of knowledge gaps (C5, C35-C36) as SUPPORTED and clearly motivating the study focus. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these gap-identification claims.
OpenEval evaluates comparison to atomoxetine studies (C118-C119) as SUPPORTED and strengthening interpretation. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate this comparative discussion.

OpenEval evaluates summary of pathway-specific LC effects in fear conditioning (C103-C112) as SUPPORTED by prior literature. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these contextual claims but Reviewer 1 does note LC heterogeneity as relevant to interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates discussion of LC organization and heterogeneity (C139-C145) as SUPPORTED by recent literature. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these claims, though Reviewer 1 mentions LC heterogeneity as a weakness requiring future investigation.

OpenEval evaluates proposed future directions for inhibition experiments (C155-C157) as SUPPORTED as reasonable next steps. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these forward-looking suggestions.
